newsitem.title: DUBAI: BankWatch gives Oman BBB minus rating.
newsitem.headline: BankWatch gives Oman BBB minus rating.

text.p: New York-based Thomson BankWatch said in a statement that it had assigned small independent oil producer Oman a BBB- sovereign risk rating and rated Oman International Bank.

It said the rating was "based on the country's strong revenues from the oil and gas sector, low inflation, manageable debt burden and low debt-servicing requirements, a stable exchange rate, mounting foreign exchange reserves, and a relatively stable political environment".
Continued tight monetary policy has kept inflation under control "with the annualised rate remaining between 2.0 and 2.5 percent", it said.
"External accounts are improving as well: most estimates put last year's current account balance in the black -- marking the first such surplus since 1990," BankWatch said.
It said foreign exchange reserves rose to nearly $1.4 billion by end-1996, equal to some three months of import cover.
"As the country's heavy investment projects get underway, however, imports are likely to accelerate, causing the trade and current account surpluses to shrink over the next few years."
BankWatch said it tempered its assessment with Oman's heavy reliance on oil and gas, which left it vulnerable to oil price swings.
It also said it assigned Oman International Bank an IC-B/C intra-country issuer rating and an LC-1 short-term local currency debt rating.
BankWatch said OIB has a dominant share of Omani customer deposits due to its unmatched local distribution network.
"While management information systems and overall automation has enabled the management team to implement improved controls, lingering problem credits from years past remain sizable.
"While the excellent core deposit base provides loyal funding, asset liquidity is much less than that of the average bank based outside of Oman," it said.
It said OIB's capital is solid and will be bolstered by an imminent share issue.
